messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: control-plane error-rate spike detected (5xx) — org-lookup downstream errors rising >6% over 3m, paging on-call. https://status.redwood.ai/inc/RC-2198 :rotating_light:
oncall-zoe: I’m on it. seeing 502/504s across API gateway to control-plane. Most traces show `org-lookup: downstream timeout` or `config-service: cache-miss` in the path. Customers reporting failed model loads and intermittent auth failures.
ryan: confirming — grafana shows auth RPC P50 P95 latency up, and org-lookup qps doubled in last 10m. Top caller = public-gateway-prod.
meera: tagging billing here — some requests to billing-service are timing out too, but error budget not yet exhausted. root seems to be canon config cache TTL changes rolled ~20m ago?
sre-lead: @meera where did that TTL change land? rollout id?
meera: it was a config rollout earlier this morning — changed default `org_ttl` from 15s -> 1s for aggressive freshness (PR #4982). A/B rolled to 40% at 08:30 and then to 100% at 09:05.
terry: That would explain cache-stampede behavior on org-lookup, causing auth to fan out to DB/billing. We’re seeing sudden increased concurrency to org-lookup which then trips our throttles and cascades 5xx.
support-alejandra: Customer impact: support logs show ~120 distinct customer API keys affected in last 15m; some calls are getting 502s and 504s on embeddings endpoints. No major revenue tier outages yet but several mid-market customers reporting degraded UX.
oncall-zoe: Triage plan: 1) revert config TTL to 15s on control-plane config-service 2) apply short-term traffic shaping from gateway to control-plane (circuit-breaker + 429 backpressure) 3) enable cache warmup + prefix caching for org-lookup 4) start paging SRE for DB/billing if errors persist.
ryan: I can run the rollback. Pushing rollback to config-service now.
meera: I’ll prepare the rollback patch and hold the promote.
incident-bot: Deploy started: config-service rollback (deploy/rollback-4982) by ryan — build bld-20240315-221.
ryan: rolled back to previous config version (org_ttl=15s). Verifying...
sre-lead: while we validate, put gateway rule in to limit concurrent control-plane calls per org id to 8 and enable immediate 429s for overflow. This prevents retry storms.
nerwork: (note: that line appears in many threads)
meera: applied gateway rate-limit rule to public-gateway-prod (token bucket, 8 concurrency).
terry: I’m enabling org-lookup local prefix cache (30s) and adding a hot-key bypass to serve cached responses when downstream is unhealthy.
ryan: Observability: error-rate started dropping within 90s of rollback and rate-limit. P50 auth latency is coming down.
support-alejandra: Support update sent to affected customers: "We're investigating elevated errors affecting some API requests; mitigation in progress. We'll follow up when fully resolved."
meera: Billing timeouts still a bit high — looks like billing-service threadpool had a short spike and some requests queued. Noting `billing-db` also shows increased reads.
sre-lead: Oncall escalation: paging DB oncall (next) — @terry take a look at billing-db connection pool, @ryan keep watching config-service. I’ll open an incident ticket RC-2198 and mark Sev3 for now pending customer impact.
incident-bot: Pager duty: paging db-oncall (db-oncall) — please acknowledge RC-2198.
oncall-zoe: acked. Handoff plan if we need to rotate: I’ll be on until 1000Z, then hand off to @ryan for damping/cleanup.
ryan: DB threadpool adjusted, reduced max-concurrency for billing reads and restarted billing-worker pool to clear queued tasks.
meera: after restart, billing latency normalized. auth/org-lookup traces show cache hit rate back to normal ~30s ago.
terry: Can we confirm customer impact window and numbers? support-alejandra do you have counts?
support-alejandra: Impact window 09:05–09:26 (21m). Affected API calls ~1.2% of total traffic in that window, ~1400 failed requests, ~123 unique customer keys. No high tier accounts reported full outage; several experienced increased errors.
sre-lead: Good. Severity assessment: degrade in control-plane causing <5% of customers impacted, partial feature degradation for mid/low tier. Downgrade to Sev4 in 30m if metrics stay normal.
oncall-zoe: Post-mitigation checks: all dashboards green for last 10m, trace sampling shows no sustained error spikes. Keeping watch for 30m.
ryan: Additional mitigation: add a short-term service-side 200 fallback for org-lookup when primary fails — return stale cached org metadata (TTL tag) as degraded response to keep upstream happy. Patch queued as hotfix.
meera: Hotfix pushed and enabled on canary; returning `X-Org-Cache: stale` header when serving stale.
terry: Logging note — add instrumentation for config TTL changes and rollout percentage so we can quickly detect similar regressions in future.
support-alejandra: Posted incident message in status page and updated customers; will prepare summary for postmortem.
sre-lead: Root cause: config change (org_ttl) lowered cache TTL causing cache stampede -> org-lookup load -> auth/billing fanout -> 5xx. Contributing factors: rollout at 100% without gradual ramp safeguards, missing automatic circuit-breaker for org hot keys, and lack of early guardrails in rollout pipeline.
oncall-zoe: Action items (owner): - add rollout guardrail to require canary > 30m + health checks before 100% (meera) - default `org_ttl` revert to 15s and add a safe lower bound (ryan) - gateway: better burst protection & hot-key fencing (sre-lead) - billing: increase read pool autoscale headroom (terry) - support: customer comms template for similar incidents (support-alejandra)
ryan: I’ll stay on watch and will hand off at 1000Z to @meera if things are stable.
incident-bot: Incident RC-2198 acknowledged and actions logged.
oncall-zoe: Handoff: handing off to @meera for post-mitigation verification and postmortem writeup. I’m signing out. :white_check_mark:
meera: taking over. I’ll run the postmortem draft and include the detection/rollout timeline, customer impact counts, and remediation tasks.
sre-lead: Thanks everyone. Filing follow-up ticket RC-2198-FW for automation and guardrails.
terry: adding runbook note: when making TTL/policy changes to config, stage with `canary_duration` and ensure `cache_warmup=true` for first rollouts.
support-alejandra: I’ll pull the incident timeline for customers and attach to the postmortem.
meera: Last note: confirmed last_message at 3418500355, moving to monitoring-only.
